reasons: The cited text (§ 14.2) squarely triggers the rule: Vendor owns bespoke Deliverables — which under § 1.4 expressly exclude Vendor Technology and know-how — and Customer gets only a revocable, non-transferable licence expiring with the Order Form term. That is a genuine critical deviation from the preferred position, not a permissible 'Vendor keeps its platform' carve-out.

The redline is directionally correct and pro-customer: it flips exclusive ownership to Customer, adds an express irrevocable present assignment from Vendor, and re-points the limited term licence at Vendor, leaving the remaining sentence structure intact.

Scope is appropriately confined — §§ 14.1, 14.3 and 14.4 already deliver Customer Data/IP retention, Vendor Technology retention with the § 13.2 perpetual licence-back, and no joint ownership, so no additional operations are required for rule completeness.

The failing minimality check (0.747 changed-character ratio on the first sentence) is inherent to reversing the direction of an ownership/assignment clause as the redline guidance directs; no surplus or unrelated language was inserted, so the edit remains as narrow as the fix allows.

The comment matches the required tone, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (Vendor ownership plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence) for negotiation.
